key_insight: Trainable quantum generative models can learn a Langevin potential rather than circuit rotations, using quantum Fokker–Planck solvers to prepare and sample probability distributions.
engineering_relevance: Physics-informed parameterization offers a route to scalable quantum generative learning for scientific distributions governed by stochastic dynamics.
method: Parameterize the Langevin potential and Hermitianize its Fokker–Planck equation.
Solve using a linear combination of cosine operators implemented through quantum singular value transformation.
Encode the stationary density’s square root and sample via computational-basis measurements.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports parameter recovery for multivariate distributions and sample-efficient, convex optimization for in-distribution targets, with circuit constructions and resource analysis.
watch_item: The trainability guarantees concern in-distribution targets; practical feasibility also depends on efficient block encoding and quantum circuit resources.
paper_title: Quantum Fokker-Planck solvers as trainable generative models
